scope: Combo, reward-summary and room-clear presentation callbacks no longer create an untracked goroutine for every event.
Delivery looks up the current, joined recipient by immutable player ID and uses the existing bounded private priority lane; no public or lossy fallback.
Callbacks do not acquire world/entity/snapshot locks. Existing world broadcasting synchronizes authoritative Resonance changes without the redundant event-specific snapshot worker.
Priority pressure retains admitted messages and closes the slow transport through existing sendSafe behavior; normal read-pump cleanup remains responsible for retirement.
No changes to earned values, reward journals, character saves, casino settlement or weekly-raid delivery.

evidence: All three event payloads reach only the current recipient's priority lane; old and unrelated clients remain empty.
Delivery completes while world and recipient snapshot locks are deliberately held.
Missing, unbound, retired, transport-closed and queue-closed recipients, plus empty identifiers/messages, reject delivery.
A two-slot fixture rejects 1,000 overflow calls without creating a new queue or replacing/reordering admitted messages.
Actual loopback WebSocket upgrade: overflowing its one-slot priority lane closes the transport before the peer's fixture timeout, without spilling into lossy state traffic.
Existing race checks retain close/producer synchronization, scene-private delivery, live Resonance synchronization and unchanged-snapshot suppression.

limits: In-memory recipient and lock fixtures plus a real loopback transport are not an authenticated latest-source process, Mongo restart, production TLS/proxy or capacity run.

The test-only goroutine observes lock completion; production private feedback itself creates no worker. Existing persistence/earned-completion background admission remains a separate unresolved bound and must not be solved by dropping earned work.
The main callback wiring is compiled but the entire startup callback path was not driven in an authenticated process by this focused check.
Owner-approved jump range, latest-source login/restart, ordered version assembly, successful CI and independent public acceptance remain required.
